established_findings.statement: Operational reliability of LLM-based NetOps systems depends principally on the surrounding orchestration, tool integrations, and verification machinery rather than the base LLM alone.
limitations: High-level surveys and system reports; empirical effect sizes vary by deployment and are task-dependent
Generality across all models/vendors is not established

established_findings.statement: Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) pipelines that interpose deterministic verifiers before accepting LLM outputs reliably detect many mechanically checkable defects and can drive automated repairs.
limitations: Evidence focuses on mechanically verifiable failure classes (compilation, schema, test-executable); semantic or policy-level errors may remain
Single-case and early evaluations; production-scale robustness not fully demonstrated

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented agents and retrieval/RAG integration improve grounding and task-specific performance in operational NetOps workflows when they provide evidence traces and domain tools.
limitations: Improvements depend on tool design and integration quality
Reported systems vary in scale and evaluation rigor (some are production reports, others are prototypes)

established_findings.statement: LLM hallucinations and adversarially crafted context (prompt/document poisoning or malicious remote tool descriptions) can induce unsafe or incorrect outputs, including actionable misconfigurations.
limitations: Attack success rates vary by model, retrieval/top-k behavior, and pipeline defenses
Quantitative impact on deployed NetOps remains under-explored in public literature

established_findings.statement: Translating natural-language operator intent into device-level network configuration using LLMs is feasible but currently attains only partial semantic correctness; common solutions combine fine-tuning, in-context examples, and iterative validation/repair.
limitations: Reported accuracy and semantic completeness vary by task scope and dataset
Many evaluations use synthetic or constrained intents rather than heterogeneous production intents

established_findings.statement: Existing benchmarks and datasets for NetOps/AIOps and related LLM tasks exist but face issues (contamination, limited coverage, and limited workflow-centered safety evaluation).
limitations: Scope and severity of contamination or coverage gaps differ across benchmarks
Some domain-specific benchmarks (logs, CTI) are mature for sub-tasks but not for end-to-end agentic evaluation

unresolved_questions.statement: What precise assurance conditions (evidence types, verifier coverage, sandboxing/replay protocols, and human oversight modalities) are sufficient to grant agentic LLM workflows authority to perform autonomous production network changes?
limitations: Question motivated by reviews and frameworks; empirical thresholds and acceptance criteria remain undetermined

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do current deterministic verifiers and validators cover semantic policy-level failure modes (policy compliance, cross-device invariants, end-to-end reachability) of LLM-generated configurations?
limitations: Available literature documents verifier utility for mechanical errors but provides limited measurement for higher-order semantic guarantees

unresolved_questions.statement: Which standardized, reproducible evaluation protocols can reliably separate a model’s generative capability from operational authority and assurance in agentic NetOps?
limitations: Several proposals exist but no community-agreed protocol for end-to-end agentic operational evaluation is established in the supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: A reproducible, contamination-resistant, workflow-centered benchmark that evaluates end-to-end agentic NetOps actions (generation, deterministic verification, high-fidelity sandbox replay, and rollback-aware scoring) is lacking in public literature.
limitations: COHORT (W7166901862) demonstrates replay-based evaluation but broader, canonical benchmarks are not yet available or standardized

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical studies measuring the effectiveness of human oversight under realistic NetOps cognitive and organizational constraints (time pressure, automation bias, multi-tasking) are limited.
limitations: Existing work analyzes governance and theoretical limits; controlled NetOps-specific experiments are sparse in the supplied set

candidate_gaps.statement: Few publicly reproducible architectures combine high-fidelity emulation (real firmware), multi-agent generation, and paired offensive replay for validating generated mitigations or configurations at scale.
limitations: COHORT and COHORT-like systems exist as prototypes; generalizability and public reproducibility remain limited

candidate_gaps.statement: Systematic metrics that quantify grounding/evidence trace quality for RAG/tool-augmented NetOps agents (beyond token-level provenance) are underdeveloped.
limitations: Surveys and tool papers propose notions of grounding; few standardized, quantitative metrics for operational assurance are present in the supplied records

excluded_claims: LLMs alone (without orchestration, tool integration, verification, and constrained authority) are sufficient to safely perform production network configuration changes.
There is no risk of hallucination, prompt poisoning, or malicious tool-description attacks affecting NetOps outputs.
Existing public benchmarks for LLM NetOps evaluation are contamination-free and fully reflect production operational safety.
